title: LightmapGI: Keep the geometric side of a hit for unocclude and bounces
body:
## Description

#99538 added transparency support to LightmapGI and made ray hits respect the material cull mode.

As part of that change, `trace_ray()` applies the material cull mode before returning whether a triangle was hit from the front or the back.

For `CULL_DISABLED` materials, this means every hit is reported as a front-face hit, so the geometric side of the triangle is lost.

This causes two problems during light baking:

- The unocclude pass can no longer detect back faces around texels located inside geometry.
- Indirect bounce rays that hit the inside of opaque double-sided geometry shade the outer side of the face instead. This can let buried texels and geometric junctions collect light from outside the volume.

This change keeps `trace_ray()` geometric and applies the material cull mode only in the callers that need the material-facing side.

As a result:

- unocclude can use the true geometric front/back side;
- shadow rays keep their existing cull and transparency behavior;
- transmission paths remain unchanged;
- transparent bounce paths remain unchanged;
- opaque back faces made visible by the material cull mode are shaded from the side the ray actually hit.

For those opaque back-face hits, the normal is flipped toward the ray, matching the renderer's back-facing fragment behavior. The direct-light texture is not sampled for that case because it contains lighting for the front side only.

This is not a revert of #99538. The transparency and cull-mode behavior introduced there is preserved.

## Testing

A synthetic LightmapGI regression suite was used before and after the change.

Test cases include:

- opaque `CULL_BACK` geometry;
- opaque double-sided geometry;
- thin double-sided opaque planes;
- transparent glass;
- colored transparent glass;
- alpha/cutout surfaces;
- double-sided alpha surfaces;
- two transparent surfaces in sequence.

Results:

- Opaque `CULL_BACK` control scenes are unchanged where expected.
- Transparent glass output is bit-identical to master.
- Colored transparent glass output is bit-identical to master.
- Two transparent surfaces in sequence are bit-identical to master.
- Alpha/cutout transmission through transparent regions is preserved.
- Invalid lighting inside opaque double-sided geometry is strongly reduced.

On the real-world regression scene, using raw lightmap output with the denoiser disabled:

- 347 / 357 buried texels that were black in Godot 4.3 recover at least 80% toward the 4.3 result.
- The previous diagnostic 4.3-style variant recovered 348 / 357, but also changed modern transparency behavior.
- The new fix preserves the modern transparent path while recovering essentially the same opaque-geometry cases.

A diagnostic build that changed only unocclude was also tested and did not fix the main leakage, confirming that the bounce-side handling is required as well.

## Notes

Thin double-sided geometry remains an edge case for the unocclude heuristic because it cannot inherently distinguish a thin plane from the inside surface of a closed volume.

This PR intentionally preserves the current transparent path rather than restoring the pre-4.4 behavior.
